media.title: Pyramidion of Iufaa
media.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1921 (21.2.66), Open Access
media.note: Four faces, each from the Met view that looks straight at it (the four colour views), matted with BiRefNet, then each mapped by an affine fit of its own measured base corners and apex onto the true face triangle (slant / base 1.416 from the catalogue dimensions; the photos measure 1.36-1.38, i.e. the camera about 14 degrees above the face normal). The four black-and-white corner views were used to check which faces adjoin. The museum's painted accession number on face A was inpainted out. Mid-tones opened slightly (gamma 0.8): the Met shot it on black. Tile order in the atlas: A scarab in the solar barque, C Iufaa kneeling under the jackal (three columns), B sun disc between adoring baboons, D Iufaa kneeling under the jackal (two columns).

# pyramid-steps A stepper that lays limestone. Each finished step is one course of a small pyramid, set block by block: the blocks come up the ramp behind the back corner, over the edge onto the working bed, and are dragged across the wet gypsum to their places, front corner first. The step you are on is the course being laid. Its bed lies open, spread with mortar, and the low sun from the left throws the new blocks' long shadows across it. The courses still to come are set out in hairline on the paper, as an elevation is drawn. Finishing the last step brings the capstone up the same way and sets it. Nothing glows or changes; it is a stone set on stone. Going back lifts the top course off again, the last block laid the first one lifted. The capstone is the Met's pyramidion of Iufaa (Dynasty 26). Every block face is a cut-out of a real Giza block, and every top is a weathered surface from Dahshur or Giza. Courses shrink upward by Petrie's measured course heights of the Great Pyramid. ```html

``` ```js import { pyramidSteps } from './pyramid-steps.js'; const steps = pyramidSteps(nav, { layout: 'tower', revisit: 'done' }); steps.next(); // lay the current course and set out the next (or the capstone after the last) steps.back(); // lift the top course off again steps.go(2); // any step (0-based); go(steps.length) = finished, capstone set steps.progress(.6); // share of the current course laid: tie it to fields filled in (the demo does) steps.current; steps.length; steps.done; steps.destroy(); // canvas, observers and listeners gone; the plain list as it was nav.addEventListener('pyramid-steps:change', (e) => e.detail); // { current, previous, complete } ``` Events (bubbling): `pyramid-steps:change` on every move, `pyramid-steps:select` when a step's label is pressed (cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps the component from moving, so your form can validate first), `pyramid-steps:laid` `{ course }` when a course's last block is home, `pyramid-steps:capstone` when the capstone settles. The last two are there for sound. Without JS, or before the stone has loaded, it is the list: numbered, current step marked. ## Options `data-*` on the element, or the options object (which wins). | Option | Attribute | Default | | |---|---|---|---| | `layout` | `data-layout` | `tower` | `tower`: the pyramid with its labels beside it, each on a hairline leader at its own course. `strip`: a small pyramid before a row of labels, for a header. | | `current` | `data-current` | the `li` with `aria-current="step"`, else 0 | Starting step, 0-based; `length` = finished. | | `progress` | `data-progress` | `.35` | Share of the current course laid at rest. | | `revisit` | `data-revisit` | `done` | Which labels are buttons: `done` steps, `all`, or `none`. The others are plain text, never disabled buttons. | | `face` | `data-face` | from the seed | Which of the capstone's four faces looks at you (0-3). | | `seed` | `data-seed` | random | Fixes the bond, the choice of stones and the capstone's turn. Use the same seed on two navs to show the same pyramid. | | `speed` | `data-speed` | `1` | Multiplies how fast blocks are hauled and set. | | `assets` | `data-assets` | `./assets/` beside the module | Where `blocks.webp`, `blocks.json`, `capstone.webp` and `mortar.webp` live. | A label that already contains an `` or a `
